unmapped: N self-interested clients in a star network; each has a data-sharing cost D^p_i and shares data only if incentive (data + monetary) exceeds cost (individual rationality)
the server knows the clients' reported data-sharing costs D^p
communication cost (number of scalars transferred) and monetary incentive cost are additional objectives
an arbitrary client is active at each time step
settings.definition_quote: At each time step $t \in [T]$, an arbitrary client $i_{t} \in [N]$ becomes active and chooses an arm $\bx_{t} $ from a candidate set $\cA_{t}\subseteq \bR^{d}$, and then receives the corresponding reward feedback $y_{t}=f(\bx_{t}) + \eta_{t} \in \bR$. Note that $\cA_{t}$ is time-varying, $f$ denotes the unknown reward function shared by all clients, and $\eta_{t}$ denotes zero mean sub-Gaussian noise with known variance $\sigma^{2}$.

conditions: applies to the specific algorithm Inc-FedUCB with payment-free incentive mechanism
at most c/(2C) * N/log(T/N) clients have cost D_i^p <= min{(1+L^2/lambda)^T, (1+T L^2/(lambda d))^d}

source.label: thm:negative_result
source.quote: When there are at most $\frac{c}{2C} \frac{N}{\log(T/N)}$ number of clients (for some constant $C,c >0$), whose cost value $D_{i}^{p} \leq \min\{(1+\frac{L^{2}}{\lambda})^{T}, (1+\frac{TL^{2}}{\lambda d})^{d} \}$, there exists a linear bandit instance with $\sigma = L = S = 1$ such that for $T \geq N d$, the expected regret for \model~algorithm with payment-free incentive mechanism is at least $\Omega(d\sqrt{NT})$.

results.notes: Derived from He et al. 2022 Theorem 5.3. Regret defined via expected rewards (pseudo-regret). C and c here are constants, not corruption.

tuning: D_c = T/(N^2 d log T) - sqrt(T^2/(N^2 d R log T)) log beta, R = ceil(d log(1+T/(lambda d)))

source.label: thm:regret_inc_feducb
source.quote: Furthermore, by setting $\beta \geq e^{-\frac{1}{N}}$, the cumulative regret is \[R_T= O\left(d\sqrt{T}\log T\right)\]

results.notes: Regret is pseudo-regret summed over all clients; the theorem says 'with high probability' and the proof holds w.p. 1-delta with delta=1/T. Heuristic search runs in O(N) per round per the paper.

tuning: D_c = T/(N^2 d log T) - sqrt(T^2/(N^2 d R log T)) log beta

source.label: thm:regret_inc_feducb
source.quote: Henceforth, the communication cost satisfies \[C_T = O(Nd^2) \cdot P = O(N^2d^3\log T)\]

results.notes: Communication cost (number of scalars). Number of epochs P = O(N d log T) (Lemma 9).

bound.expression_latex: M_{T} = O\left ( \max D^p \cdot P \cdot N - \sum\limits_{i = 1}^N P_i \cdot \left ( \frac{\det(\lambda I)}{\det(V_T)}\right) ^{\frac{1}{P_i}}  \right)

symbols.D_p_max: maximum client data-sharing cost max_i D^p_i
symbols.P: total number of epochs, O(N d log T)
symbols.Psi: sum_i P_i (det(lambda I)/det(V_T))^(1/P_i), P_i = number of epochs client i is paid

tuning: D_c = T/(N^2 d log T) - sqrt(T^2/(N^2 d R log T)) log beta

source.label: thm:regret_inc_feducb
source.quote: Under threshold $\beta$ and clients' committed data sharing cost $D^p = \{D^p_1, \cdots, D^p_N\}$, with high probability the monetary incentive cost of \model~satisfies~ $$M_{T} = O\left ( \max D^p \cdot P \cdot N - \sum\limits_{i = 1}^N P_i \cdot \left ( \frac{\det(\lambda I)}{\det(V_T)}\right) ^{\frac{1}{P_i}}  \right) $$

results.notes: Monetary incentive (payment) cost, not regret. Proof concludes M_T = O(N^2 d log T) treating D_p_max as constant.
